slides.title: Where fiber climbs the pole
slides.sub: Pole risers, U-guards and building risers

slides.title: The first 8 feet up a pole is where cables get hit.
slides.body: Mowers, vehicles and curious hands all reach that far.

slides.title: Why cables climb poles
slides.body: Underground feeders meet aerial side streets. The cable leaves the duct through a long sweep and rises to the comms space.

slides.title: The code wants protection
slides.body: In the US, the NESC requires mechanical protection where cable on a pole could be damaged, typically to about 8 feet.

slides.title: Size conduit for tomorrow
slides.body: Adding cable to riser conduit means pulling through the pipe. Size it for future cables from day one.

slides.title: Building risers have rules
slides.body: US code wants riser-rated OFNR cable, or plenum OFNP in air-handling space. Fire-stop every floor penetration.

A few feet of hardware at the base of a pole protects thousands of feet of cable either side of it.

That is the riser: where fiber leaves the ground and climbs to the comms space. Swipe for U-guard vs riser conduit, and the building riser rules people forget.
